answer: An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the vault index resolves every citation against the zephyr checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the sparrow audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 135 aliases thus pays the authoring cost 135 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 7 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
